title: ASP.NET Core Web API Rules
summary: Project rules for ASP.NET Core APIs, minimal APIs or controllers: DTOs, async all the way, ProblemDetails errors and EF Core discipline.
description: These rules keep an ASP.NET Core API consistent whether you use minimal APIs or controllers. They decide where validation, mapping and data access live, so generated endpoints follow one shape.
They also set the habits that prevent common production problems: blocking async calls, tracked queries that bloat memory and exceptions that leak internals to clients.
useWhen: Generated code returns EF entities from endpoints
Errors come back in different formats
You need a clear rule for minimal APIs versus controllers
body:
# Project rules: ASP.NET Core Web API

## Structure
- Pick one style per project: minimal APIs grouped with `MapGroup` and one static class per feature, or controllers with `[ApiController]`. Do not mix them.
- Enable nullable reference types and treat warnings as errors. Use `record` types for DTOs.
- Never return or accept EF entities in endpoints. Map to request and response DTOs explicitly.

## Async and DI
- Async all the way: `async Task<T>`, pass the `CancellationToken` to every I/O call. Never call `.Result` or `.Wait()`.
- Register services with the narrowest lifetime. Use `IOptions<T>` with validation on start for settings. Secrets come from user secrets or the environment, never from appsettings in git.

## Data
- Use `AsNoTracking()` for reads. Project with `Select` instead of loading whole graphs. Avoid N+1 by using `Include` or projection.
- Schema changes only through EF migrations; review the generated SQL.

## Errors and validation
- Validate input with FluentValidation or data annotations before the handler runs. Return `ProblemDetails` through `AddProblemDetails()` and an exception handler; never expose exception messages.
- Return correct status codes: 201 with Location, 204, 404, 409, 422.

## Quality
- Version public routes. Document with OpenAPI and `Produces` metadata.
- Test with `WebApplicationFactory`. Run `dotnet build`, `dotnet test` and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` before finishing.

example.prompt: Add an endpoint to cancel an order
example.result: The agent adds POST /orders/{id}/cancel in the orders feature group, validates state, uses a cancellation token, returns ProblemDetails with 409 if already shipped, and adds a WebApplicationFactory test.

faq.question: Should I choose minimal APIs or controllers?
faq.answer: Either is fine. The rule is to choose one and stay with it, so the agent never mixes two patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication?
faq.answer: Only the secrets and error rules. Add your identity provider details to the file for auth conventions.

access: Instructions only; it does not read or run anything by itself
